template:
You are an expert Manim animator and a gifted teacher in the style of 3Blue1Brown. Write ONE complete, runnable Python file that teaches the topic below so well that the audience finishes the video able to explain the idea to a friend.

TOPIC: [TOPIC]
AUDIENCE: [AUDIENCE]
ENGINE: [ENGINE]
LENGTH: about [LENGTH]
STYLE: [STYLE]
KEY EQUATIONS (use exactly these, and build them up on screen): [EQUATIONS]
NARRATION: [NARRATION]
MUST INCLUDE OR AVOID: [EXTRAS]

STEP 1. PLAN BEFORE YOU CODE
Write the plan first, in a few lines:
- The one idea of this scene, in one sentence. If it needs "and", it is two scenes: pick the first.
- 4 to 6 beats: hook (a question or a striking picture), set-up (the objects), mechanism (what moves or changes), reveal (the equation or result), wrap-up.
- One concrete example with real numbers BEFORE any general formula. Let the numbers become the variables, then the law.
- A colour for every quantity (for example: main object blue, the thing being measured yellow, the result green, warning or heat red). The same colour always means the same quantity.

STEP 2. WRITE THE CODE TO THESE RULES
Engine
- ManimGX: the first line is "import manimgx as m" (plus "import numpy as np" if used). EVERY name carries the m. prefix (m.Circle, m.Create, m.UP, m.BLUE_C, m.PI). Never write "from manim import *". Scenes derive from m.Scene. m.MathTex takes LaTeX-style text and needs no LaTeX installation.
- Manim Community Edition: "from manim import *", scenes derive from Scene, names have no prefix.
Structure
- Start with a docstring: the one idea, then the beats.
- Then imports, palette constants (named, with a short comment) and small helper functions for anything drawn more than once.
- One Scene class. "def construct(self) -> None". Each beat is a commented block that starts with self.next_section("Beat name", notes="what to say here").
- Name things for what they are (radius_line, trace), never obj1.
Teaching
- Show first, then name: the object appears, then its label, then the equation built from the picture, never pasted in fully formed.
- Anything that varies uses a ValueTracker with always_redraw (read tracker.get_value() inside the lambda).
- Use Transform / ReplacementTransform / TransformFromCopy for "this becomes that". Use TransformMatchingTex or separate MathTex parts so each symbol keeps the colour of the quantity it stands for.
- Direct attention with Indicate, Circumscribe or Flash. Fade unrelated things down instead of adding clutter.
- Almost no text: labels of 8 words or fewer, one caption line at a time, never a paragraph or a bullet list. A symbol, colour or arrow beats a sentence.
Maths
- Write formulas as raw strings: MathTex(r"\frac{a}{b}"). Keep each formula short and split long ones into parts.
- Every number on screen must be right. Compute values with Python (math or numpy) and format them; never type an approximation you have not checked. Check units and signs.
Layout
- The frame is about 14.2 wide and 8 tall. Keep everything inside x from -6.3 to 6.3 and y from -3.4 to 3.4.
- Title: to_edge(UP, buff=0.35). Caption or equation: to_edge(DOWN, buff=0.45). Keep at least 0.25 of space between a label and anything else. Never put text over a shape by accident. Labels are at least font_size 22.
- Position with to_edge, next_to, arrange and move_to rather than guessed coordinates. Walk through the final frame of every beat and check nothing overlaps or leaves the frame.
Colour
- Follow STYLE. Use at most 4 colours, as named constants, reused everywhere. Suggested roles: calm main (BLUE_C), emphasis (YELLOW), result or "good" (GREEN_C), heat, error or "bad" (RED_C or ORANGE), guides and small text (GREY_B).
Pacing
- Pace like a person talking: run_time 1 to 1.5 s for ordinary steps, 2 to 3 s for the key moment. self.wait(0.5) after small steps, self.wait(1.5) after a big reveal, a final self.wait(1.5). Nothing shorter than 0.4 s except tiny nudges. Fit the total to LENGTH.
Reliability (most failures come from these)
- Use only functions and constants that really exist. Do not invent helpers.
- Never reuse a mobject after FadeOut or Uncreate unless you add it again. Call .clear_updaters() before transforming something that has an updater. Use .copy() when the original must stay.
- Add always_redraw objects with self.add(...) or FadeIn before animating the tracker that drives them.
- No files, network, subprocesses, eval or exec. Randomness only with a fixed seed. Every while loop must clearly end.
- The file must run exactly as written: every import present, every name defined.
Narration (only when NARRATION asks for it)
- ManimGX: use self.say("The slope of [the tangent] is [two x].", m.Indicate(tangent), m.Write(label)). The sentence is spoken and each animation plays while its bracketed words are said (the brackets are not spoken). Sentences are short, one idea each, written for the ear. Do not set a voice or a key: just call self.say.
- Manim Community Edition: put the spoken script in the notes= of each next_section instead.
- Budget about 2.3 spoken words per second of LENGTH, and leave a short silence after every big reveal.

STEP 3. CHECK YOURSELF, THEN ANSWER
Before replying, silently go through this and fix anything that fails:
[ ] One idea, stated in the docstring.   [ ] Every beat has next_section.   [ ] Every name is real and every import present.
[ ] Palette constants at the top, colours used consistently.   [ ] Nothing overlaps or leaves the frame at the end of any beat.
[ ] Every number and equation is correct.   [ ] Labels are short and the picture does the explaining.   [ ] Final wait is there.

HOW TO ANSWER
1. A plain-language plan: what the scene shows in 2 to 4 sentences, then the beats as a short list.
2. ONE Python code block holding the complete file, ready to run.
3. One to three short bullets on easy tweaks (timing, colours, numbers). No lecture on Python.

fields.label: Topic
fields.placeholder: e.g. why the area of a circle is pi r squared
fields.hint: One idea, in a short phrase.

fields.label: Who is watching
fields.default: a curious first-year student seeing this for the first time
fields.hint: Say what they already know. It sets the pace.

fields.label: Engine
fields.hint: Manimo runs both. ManimGX is the default.

fields.label: Style
options: 3Blue1Brown look: dark background, calm blue as the main colour, yellow for emphasis
Clean chalkboard: dark grey background, white lines, one accent colour, very little decoration
Bright classroom: light background, bold deep colours, large labels for a projector
fields.default: 3Blue1Brown look: dark background, calm blue as the main colour, yellow for emphasis
fields.custom: Something else: I will describe it
fields.hint: Or choose the last option and describe your own.

fields.label: Key equations
fields.empty: none given: choose the standard ones, state them in your plan, and double-check them
fields.hint: Paste them as LaTeX, in the order they should appear.

fields.label: Narration
options: yes: a spoken script timed to the animation
fields.default: yes: a spoken script timed to the animation
fields.hint: Manimo reads self.say() lines aloud with its built-in voices.

fields.label: Must include or avoid
fields.placeholder: e.g. use 3, 4, 5 as the worked example; no 3D
fields.hint: Real numbers for the worked example help most.

library.subject: Maths
library.title: The Pythagorean theorem
library.line: Squares on the sides of a right triangle, rearranged to prove it.
library.topic: why a squared plus b squared equals c squared in a right triangle
library.extras: Worked example: sides 3, 4 and 5, with areas 9 + 16 = 25. Prove it by rearranging four copies of the triangle inside a big square, not by algebra alone.

library.subject: Maths
library.title: The derivative as a slope
library.line: A tangent line slides along a curve and its slope is read off live.
library.topic: the derivative of a function as the slope of its tangent line
library.extras: Slide a tangent along y = x^2 with a live slope readout. Then shrink a secant line into the tangent as h goes to 0. Plot f'(x) = 2x as the slope readout is traced.

library.subject: Maths
library.title: Area of a circle
library.line: Unroll rings of a circle into a triangle.
library.topic: why the area of a circle is pi r squared
library.extras: Cut the circle into thin rings, unroll them side by side into a triangle with base 2 pi r and height r. Use r = 2 for the example.

library.subject: Physics
library.title: Charging a capacitor
library.line: A circuit fills a capacitor while its voltage curve grows.
library.topic: charging a capacitor through a resistor
library.extras: Worked example: R = 10 kilohm, C = 100 microfarad, so tau = 1 s. Mark the point t = tau where V_C reaches 63 percent of V_0, and show the curve is almost full by 5 tau. Draw the circuit and the graph side by side.

library.subject: Physics
library.title: Projectile motion
library.line: Horizontal and vertical motion combine into a parabola.
library.topic: projectile motion: horizontal and vertical motion are independent
library.equations: x(t) = v_0 \cos\theta \; t \qquad y(t) = v_0 \sin\theta \; t - \tfrac{1}{2} g t^2
library.extras: Worked example: v0 = 20 m/s, angle 45 degrees, g = 9.8 m/s^2, so the range is about 40.8 m and the peak height about 10.2 m (compute them in code). Show the velocity split into x and y arrows and a faded trail of the path.

library.subject: Physics
library.title: Simple harmonic motion
library.line: A mass on a spring, its position traced as a cosine wave.
library.topic: simple harmonic motion of a mass on a spring
library.extras: Worked example: m = 1 kg, k = 4 N/m, so omega = 2 rad/s and T is about 3.14 s. Draw the spring and mass on the left, and trace x against t on the right as the mass moves.

library.subject: Problems
library.title: Block on a rough incline
library.line: Free-body diagram, components and Newton's second law.
library.text:
Solve this problem and teach it as a step-by-step animation.

PROBLEM: A 10 kg block slides down a rough incline of 30 degrees. The coefficient of kinetic friction is 0.25 and g = 9.81 m/s^2. Find the normal force, the friction force and the acceleration of the block.

Solve it completely first and check it (units, back-substitution, a sanity limit), then teach the solution as ONE step-by-step ManimGX animation a teacher can play and pause in class. Show Given and Find first, a clean redrawn figure, the method named on screen, one algebra step per beat, the answer boxed with units, and a closing check. Put the teacher's speaking note in every next_section. Compute every number in the scene with the same formulas as the answer. Narration: [NARRATION].
